'''Pavlos G. Lagoudakis''' is a Greek and Russian physicist. He is a Distinguished Professor and Provost at the [[Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology]] (Skoltech).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Pavlos Lagoudakis |url=https://skoltech.ru/en/persons/lagudakis-pavlos |access-date=2025-12-11 |website=skoltech.ru |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Lagoudakis completed his undergraduate studies (B.Sc. in Physics) at the [[University of Athens]], Greece, graduating in 2000. He was awarded his Doctor of Philosophy (PhD in Physics) in 2003 from the [[University of Southampton]],<ref>[https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/465045/1/906216.pdf University of Southampton Institutional Research Repository, ePrints Soton]</ref> United Kingdom. During his postgraduate research he investigated the physics of exciton-polaritons in semiconductor microcavities under the supervision of [[Jeremy Baumberg]].<ref>[https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/pssb.200560960 Baumberg, J. J., & Lagoudakis, P. G. (2005). Parametric amplification and polariton liquids in semiconductor microcavities. physica status solidi (b), 242(11), 2210-2223.]</ref> He subsequently conducted postdoctoral research at [[LMU Munich]], Germany,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alumni - Photonics and Optoelectronics Group - LMU Munich |url=https://www.phog.physik.uni-muenchen.de/people/alumni/index.html |access-date=2025-12-11 |website=www.phog.physik.uni-muenchen.de |language=en}}</ref> focusing on the optoelectronic properties of organic semiconductors and colloidal nanoparticles.

== Academic career ==
In 2006, Lagoudakis was awarded a Roberts Fellowship and joined the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Southampton, UK, as a lecturer. In 2008, he was appointed to a personal chair (2008-2024) and later became Director for Research in the Department of Physics and Astronomy (2013–2019).<ref>{{Cite journal |date=September 2017 |title=Guest Editorial: Introduction to the JSTQE Issue on Semiconductor Nanocrystal Optoelectronics |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8048562/ |journal=IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics |volume=23 |issue=5 |pages=1–3 |doi=10.1109/JSTQE.2017.2753079 |issn=1558-4542|url-access=subscription |hdl=11693/37986 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> Between 2011 and 2014, he chaired the University’s Nanoscience Research Strategy Group. Between 2013-2014, he was a visiting professor at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]], Switzerland. In 2008, he was awarded a JSPS academic research fellowship at the [[University of Hokkaido]], Japan, where he collaborated with Oliver Wright.<ref>[https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.103.L241201 Li, C., Harley, R. T., Lagoudakis, P. G., Wright, O. B., & Matsuda, O. (2021). Coherent phonon detection gated by transient spin-polarized electrons. Physical Review B, 103(24), L241201]</ref> In 2016, he established the Hybrid Photonics Laboratory at Skoltech.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hybrid Photonics Lab |url=https://skoltech.ru/en/laboratories/hybrid-photonics-labs-hpl |access-date=2025-12-11 |website=skoltech.ru |language=en-US}}</ref> Between 2024 and 2025, Lagoudakis has served as a [[Distinguished Professor]],<ref name=":0" /> Director of the Center for Photonic Science and Engineering,<ref>[https://www.skoltech.ru/en/center/photonics Website of the Skoltech Center for Photonic Science and Engineering]</ref> and Senior Vice President for Basic Research at Skoltech. Since 2025, Lagoudakis is serving as Provost for Research and Education at Skoltech.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
Lagoudakis’s research spans light–matter interactions, hybrid photonic systems, and quantum fluids of light.<ref>{{Cite web |title=www.polaritonics.org - Our Team |url=https://sites.google.com/view/polaritonics/our-team |access-date=2025-12-11 |website=sites.google.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
* [[IUPAP]] Young Scientist Prize in Quantum Electronics (2011) – for contributions to polaritonics and hybrid photonics<ref>[https://archive2.iupap.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/file_53171.pdf Announcement by IUPAP]</ref>
* VYZOV Prize for Future Technologies (2023) – for pioneering work in polariton-based computing and creation of optical transistors<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pavlos Lagoudakis |url=https://vyzovaward.ru/en/laureates/pavlos_lagoudakis/ |access-date=2025-12-11 |website=vyzovaward.ru}}</ref>

== Affiliations ==
* [[Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology]] – Distinguished Professor, Director of the Center for Photonic Science & Engineering, Provost for Research and Education.
* [[University of Southampton]] – Former Professor of Physics, Department of Physics and Astronomy.
